rows.title: Good food and stable housing have huge effects on health. So Colorado Medicaid wants to cover those, too.
rows.standfirst: Colorado is following about 20 other states in asking the federal government if the state-federal health insurance program can cover meals and rent

rows.title: Colorado now has the worst outbreak of bird flu among dairy cattle in the country
rows.standfirst: The state has seen nearly one-quarter of its herds affected, most in the past month

rows.title: Colorado awarded $40.5 million federal quantum technology grant to become worldwide hub
rows.standfirst: CU Boulder and Colorado businesses will benefit as the state becomes one of 12 new federal technology hubs as part of a competitive funding sprint in emerging ideas

rows.title: Tri-State set to pay $70M in aid to Moffat County, city of Craig to offset impact of closing power plant, coal mines
rows.standfirst: Settlement negotiated by city, county and state utility advocates is short of the $118M requested, but includes a hand off of valuable water storage rights

rows.title: Plan to drill 155 oil and gas wells near Lowry landfill in Aurora gets endorsement of top regulator
rows.standfirst: Lowry Ranch neighbors say they won’t stop fighting the Crestone drilling plan submitted 20 months ago. Approval, they say, would put ECMC in violation of its own mission to protect public safety.

rows.title: New workforce housing and creative space opens in Mancos
rows.standfirst: Brand new Mancos Commons building combines crucial units of affordable housing with space for artistic programming

rows.title: No, the EPA’s ozone-fighting mandate did not sharply raise Colorado gas prices
rows.standfirst: Entering Fourth of July driving boom, Front Range gas prices are lower than a year ago despite requirement for “reformulated gas” that reduces ozone-causing emissions

rows.title: New law will make it tougher for Colorado HOAs to foreclose on homes
rows.standfirst: The measure is aimed in part at making good on a promise from the governor and lawmakers to change the state’s HOA laws following a Colorado Sun investigation last year

rows.title: Nearly 1.8 million chickens will be culled in the latest bird flu outbreak at a Colorado poultry farm
rows.standfirst: Gov. Jared Polis declared a disaster emergency for the egg-laying operation in Weld County

rows.title: Xcel should be ordered to get moving on home solar hookups, state regulators and industry groups say
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s largest utility promised 8 months ago to set fees, deadlines, procedures and a connection timeline but has not delivered

rows.title: What’s Working: Despite setbacks, a Durango builder is framing affordable houses in under a month
rows.standfirst: With high-end modular building, Higher Purpose Homes hope to increase affordability by speeding up supply. Plus: 62,000 Colorado workers get paid family leave, June home sales, more!

rows.title: Colorado identifies three new human cases of bird flu and more people are symptomatic
rows.standfirst: The new cases are linked to a poultry farm in Weld County. Health officials say risk to the general public remains low.

rows.title: Recycling can feel pointless. Here are Colorado companies changing that.
rows.standfirst: The idea of recycling is nice. But with few companies recycling consumer waste into something useful, efforts seem futile. Don’t despair. Here are companies making new stuff out of old stuff in Colorado.

rows.title: Colorado is steering affordable housing money to the middle class — and away from the working poor
rows.standfirst: Using affordable housing dollars once reserved exclusively for low-income residents, the state of Colorado has begun subsidizing rental units for middle-income families who make as much as $170,000

rows.title: Xcel Energy is unsure it can meet Colorado’s clean-energy goals at the cost it promised
rows.standfirst: The utility wants more time, but regulators and consumer advocates worry delays will only boost the $12 billion price tag even higher

rows.title: Widespread technology outage disrupts hundreds of flights at Denver airport, law enforcement systems
rows.standfirst: Cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike said it does not suspect a security incident or cyberattack

rows.title: What’s Working: Repurposing old stuff in Colorado can be profitable
rows.standfirst: “Industrial thrift store” finds growth in rethinking old big things. Plus: What’s getting recycled in Colorado, Aurora attracts $600 million nicotine plant, latest job data, layoffs and more!

rows.title: Garlic from this Colorado farm is making neighbors give up grocery store bulbs for good
rows.standfirst: Green Acres U-Pick, operated by Bob and Elaine Korver, cultivates a globe-spanning collection of garlics that most home cooks have never encountered.

rows.title: Extreme heat in Colorado may have contributed to an extraordinary outbreak of bird flu in people
rows.standfirst: High temperatures made it harder for workers handling infected chickens to wear PPE. Six later tested positive.

rows.title: Lawsuits challenging Summit County regulation of short-term rentals dismissed by federal courts
rows.standfirst: Homeowners in Summit County last year sued to overturn recent regulations limiting permits and annual bookings as well as increasing taxes on short-term rentals

rows.title: Demand for Colorado’s paid-family and medical leave 44% less than expected
rows.standfirst: Six months into the new FAMLI program, more than 62,000 Colorado workers received a total of $311 million. The amount is 44% less than projected. Most have returned to work.

rows.title: EPA grants $328 million for Colorado programs designed to slash greenhouse gas emissions
rows.standfirst: The sum was split between two agencies and will be handed out to programs including green-energy workforce development and cleaning up commercial building emissions

rows.title: Two Coloradans join first-ever commercial spacewalk to research ways for people to live on Mars
rows.standfirst: The four-person crew of Polaris Dawn plans to conduct nearly 40 science experiments that could help regular people with regular health problems live on the moon or Mars

rows.title: Colorado expands testing for bird flu at dairy farms as state hits 30 cases in 30 days
rows.standfirst: The mandatory testing order for dairy cattle is an effort to stem Colorado’s worst-in-the-nation outbreak of avian influenza

rows.title: Did Colorado home values rise significantly in 2023?
rows.standfirst: Colorado residential property values jumped 26.9% statewide in 2023, with many counties reporting much higher surges.

rows.title: FTC chair, Colorado AG pledge to crack down on “abusive and predatory practices” of corporate landlords
rows.standfirst: The tenant roundtable focused on hidden fees, habitability and rent-setting algorithms accused of driving up the cost of housing

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado top-paying and lowest-paying jobs
rows.standfirst: The state’s annual wage data report is out, providing workers a better idea of how much jobs pay. Plus: Wages still growing, FAMLI update, Denver janitors vote to strike, and more!

rows.title: The Colorado community of Stagecoach is paradise to its residents. A luxury resort could turn it upside down.
rows.standfirst: The same developers that turned Big Sky, Montana, into a resort town for billionaires are moving ahead with plans to bring luxury homes and a golf course to northwestern Colorado. Those who live there are raising concerns.

rows.title: Neighbors’ last shot at stopping oil and gas drilling near Aurora Reservoir is to be declared “affected persons”
rows.standfirst: Families who live and recreate in the area are maneuvering for legal standing in hearings about Crestone’s Lowry Ranch plan to drill 166 wells under land in Aurora and Arapahoe County

rows.title: Lowry Ranch neighbors allowed to testify in hearings about oil and gas drilling near Aurora Reservoir
rows.standfirst: “Affected person” status granted to 12 families, despite Crestone Peak pointing out that none of them live within 2,000 feet of drilling sites
